name: VictoriaLogs
tagline: Log database from the VictoriaMetrics team: schemaless ingestion, LogsQL and low RAM and disk use.
description: VictoriaLogs stores and queries structured and plain-text logs with an emphasis on operational simplicity: one binary, no schema, no index tuning, and every field searchable without declaring it. It ingests the Elasticsearch bulk API, Loki push, OpenTelemetry, syslog and JSON lines, and is queried with LogsQL, a pipe-based language with word and phrase filters, field extraction and stats. A cluster mode (vlinsert, vlstorage, vlselect) adds horizontal scale. It works well as a replacement for Elasticsearch- or Loki-based log stacks when you want fast search over high-cardinality fields like trace or user IDs without running a heavyweight inverted index.

pricing.notes: Free and open source; enterprise support and features are sold by VictoriaMetrics.

scale.notes: Single node handles terabytes per day on one machine; cluster mode spreads storage across vlstorage nodes.

strengths: Every field is queryable without schema or mapping changes
Fast searches on high-cardinality fields such as trace_id or user_id
Much lower RAM and disk than Elasticsearch for the same log volume
Accepts Elasticsearch, Loki and OTLP ingestion, so existing shippers need only a URL change
Single binary with built-in web UI and live tailing
weaknesses: LogsQL is another query language to learn; no SQL
Stores data on local disk rather than object storage
Younger ecosystem than Elasticsearch or Loki for dashboards and alerting integrations
No relevance-ranked search; it filters rather than scores
useCases: Replacing an ELK stack to cut cost
Debugging by trace or request ID across services
